claims.claim_text: Minerals are the currency of life — the body's basic functions depend on them, and Wallach argues the medical profession ignores this truth to the point past the absurd.
claims.verbatim: Simply said, minerals are the currency of life. The medical profession ignores this truth to the point past the absurd

claims.claim_text: The basic functions of life cannot be performed without minerals — either as a structural part of the function or as a catalytic cofactor (for RNA, DNA, sub-cellular and digestive enzymes, and the utilization of vitamins).
claims.verbatim: The basic functions of life itself cannot be performed without minerals, either as a major part of the function or as a catalytic cofactor

claims.claim_text: Wallach frames heat-stroke deaths (he points to the deadly July 1993 US east-coast heat wave) as a simple salt/sodium deficiency — easily remedied with water and salt, and worsened by doctor-ordered low-salt diets.
claims.verbatim: a simple salt or sodium deficiency (your basic heat stroke that any boy scout could diagnose and recognize and remedy with water and salt

a trace mineral, Selenium, in the etiology and

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites U.S. Senate Document 264 (1936) and the 1992 Rio Earth Summit report on soil mineral-depletion rates: the world's farm and range soils are 'anemic' — soils that should contain 60 elements have few or none.
claims.verbatim: U.S Senate Document 264 (1936) and the 1992 Earth Summit Report (Rio) on mineral depletion rates of the world's farm and range soils point out graphically that our Earth's soils are anemic - the soil should contain 60 of them, there are few or none

claims.verbatim: It is not the reduced calorie level that gave the rats their extended life spans by 30, 40 and 50%, but rather it is the increased concentration of mineral per calorie in the diet

claims.claim_text: The human population's doubling time has collapsed — 100,000 years before written history, 700 years after the dawn of agriculture, and only 35 to 40 years today — intensifying the competition for the body's basic raw materials.
claims.verbatim: Before written history, it took 100,000 years to double the Earth’s human populations; after the dawn of agriculture, (5,000 to 8,000 years ago) it took 700 years to double the population of human kind; today at the brink of the 21st century, it takes only 35 to 40 years to double our numbers!

claims.claim_text: The 75.5-year average American lifespan is only 62% of the human genetic potential for longevity of 120 to 140 years and ranks 17th among industrialized nations — falling as much as 50% short of that potential.
claims.verbatim: The 75.5 year average life span for Americans places us at 17th in longevity when we are compared with the other industrialized nations and this level of boastful “success” falls far short (as much as 50% short) of our human genetic potential for longevity of 120 to 140 years.

claims.claim_text: Popular health movements — vegetarianism, macrobiotics, biofeedback, meditation, exercise, yoga, free medical care — have not extended the American lifespan beyond 75.5 years, only 62% of the 120-to-140-year genetic potential.
claims.verbatim: evangelize vegetarianism, macrobiotics, biofeedback, meditation, exercise, pure thought, yoga and free medical care for all (usually vote-buying politicians!); yet none of these practices have extended the human lifespan in America to more than 75.5 years- only 62% of our human genetic potential for longevity of 120 to 140 years.

claims.claim_text: The full complement of 90 essential nutrients once present in Earthly foods is no longer reliably there — either totally absent or so highly variable that obtaining them from food alone is a gamble.
claims.verbatim: Unfortunately, the entire complement of the 90 essential nutrients required for optimal health and longevity historically found in our Earthly foods are no longer there - they are either totally absent or their availability is so highly variable that your chances of obtaining them from food alone is more of a gamble than a Las Vegas “crap-shoot”!!!

claims.claim_text: Genetic potential is meaningless without the basic mineral raw materials to support development and maintenance — Wallach likens engineered flesh without minerals to running a Mercedes with no oil or coolant.
claims.verbatim: genetic potential without the basic raw materials to support the process of development and extended maintenance of the flesh is inherently faulty in its premise!!

claims.claim_text: Wallach identifies ancient, diverse cultures that reach the 120-to-140-year longevity potential disease-free — Tibetans, Russian Georgians, Armenians, Azerbaijanis, Abkhazians, Hunzakuts, Vilcabambas, the Titicacas — through access to plant-derived colloidal minerals (rare earths).
claims.verbatim: If you access and plug into the plant derived RARE EARTHS used for thousands of years by certain tribes of Tibetans, Russian Georgians, Armenians, Azerbaijanies, Abkhazians, Hunzakuts, Vilcabambas or the Titicacas you can make it too!!!

claims.claim_text: Mineral supplementation is a necessity of life — since before recorded history humans craved and consumed minerals (major minerals, trace minerals, and rare earths) as clays, salts, animal tissue, and colloidal-mineral-rich plants.
claims.verbatim: Minerals and mineral supplements to our meals are in fact a necessity of life. Since before recorded history man craved and consciously consumed minerals including the major minerals, trace minerals and Rare Earths in the form of clays, salts, animal tissue (bones and meat) or colloidal mineral rich plants.

claims.claim_text: Wallach rejects the medical advice to eat little or no salt — sodium is a craved necessity, evidenced by the salt block every rancher provides livestock and the snack-food industry that profits from the craving.
claims.verbatim: Physicians would have you believe that you need little or no salt (they must think we’re dumber than cows for the first food item a good husbandryman puts out for his livestock is a salt block!!); however, the multibillion dollar a year snack food industry is well aware of your need and craving for salt and other minerals.

claims.claim_text: Wallach attributes the July 1993 East Coast heat-wave deaths to salt/sodium deficiency caused by physician-prescribed low- or no-salt diets for high blood pressure and heart disease; those successfully treated received IV saline.
claims.verbatim: The human tragedy of the heat wave of ’93 was a direct result of the allopathic doctors who put their charges (their patients) on reduced or salt free diets for high blood pressure or heart disease.

claims.claim_text: Of the 75 metals on the periodic chart — all detected in human blood and body fluids — at least 60 have physiological value for humans, and not a single function in the body can take place without at least one mineral or metal cofactor.
claims.verbatim: There are 75 metals listed in the periodic chart, all of which have been detected in human blood and other body fluids - we know that at least 60 of these metals (minerals) have physiological value for man. Organically not a single function in the human body can take place without at least one mineral or metal cofactor.

claims.claim_text: Wallach recommends adding lithium to the public water supply and eliminating fluoride; conventional medicine confines lithium to psychiatric use (manic depression).
claims.verbatim: The current medical use of lithium is limited to psychiatric patients, especially manic depression. We would like to see lithium added to the public water supply and eliminate fluoride!!!

claims.claim_text: The Earth's soils are "anemic" — mining, deforestation, farming, irrigation, and acid rain have shifted, eroded, and leached the life-sustaining minerals from once mineral-rich land.
claims.verbatim: Our Earth is anemic!!!! A potentially apocalyptic mixture of mining, deforestation, farming, irrigation and acid rain has shifted, eroded or leached our life giving and life-sustaining raw materials from our formerly mineral rich land.

claims.claim_text: Remineralizing the Earth's depleted farmland is technically possible but, as a realistic project, an economic impossibility.
claims.verbatim: To remineralize the Earth is technically possible but as a realistic project would be an economic impossibility.

claims.claim_text: Minerals are unevenly distributed in soil — croplands hold no uniform blanket of minerals but veins (like chocolate swirls in ripple ice cream), so relying on food alone for minerals is a risky gamble.
claims.verbatim: It is obvious that minerals are not equally distributed in soils. The scary part is that fields where our food crops are grown do not contain a uniform blanket of minerals, if they contain any nutritional minerals at all, they occur in veins much like the chocolate swirls found in chocolate ripple ice cream - at best depending solely on getting minerals from food grown in soil is a very risky crap shoot!!

claims.claim_text: Minerals are more fundamental than vitamins: the body can make some use of minerals without vitamins, but lacking minerals, vitamins are useless. (Wallach reproduces this within his U.S. Senate Document 264 discussion.)
claims.verbatim: Lacking vitamins, the system can make some use of minerals, but lacking minerals, vitamins are useless.

claims.claim_text: Modern NPK fertilizer replaces only three elements, so cropping "mines" the soil's minerals within 5 to 10 years and irrigation speeds the leaching — after 100+ years the result is rising rates of degenerative disease.
claims.verbatim: It only takes 5 to 10 years for agriculture to “mine” the minerals from the soil by cropping. Irrigation while providing water for increased production in terms of tons and bushels actually speeds up the leaching of nutritional minerals from the land
